author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Kearsarge Regional School Board has set a long-term goal of operating two elementary schools, recommending the eventual closure of Simonds Elementary in Warner and Sutton Central in Bradford.

Superintendent Michael Bessette told families that the target would be implemented in summer 2028 and would not affect the 2026-27 school year. A final closure cannot be made by the board alone: voters in the affected communities would have to approve the plan. A citizen petition could bring the issue to a vote sooner.

District leaders cited major repair needs, taxpayer costs and the challenge of maintaining very small classes across several buildings. Consolidation could concentrate students and staff while limiting future capital spending, but the proposal has drawn concern from parents and residents who said they learned of the recommendation with little warning.

The board’s action establishes a planning direction, not an immediate shutdown order. Enrollment, transportation, staffing, building conditions and the use of any closed properties will require further public review. Families should expect additional meetings and formal votes before the district can move from recommendation to implementation.
dek: The regional school board recommends closing Simonds Elementary and Sutton Central as part of a long-term consolidation plan, with local votes still required.
headline: Kearsarge board targets two-school elementary model by summer 2028
